ledger.note: 1515: 'Biswa Singha announced himself the king of Kamata bounded on the east by Barnadi River' and on the west by the Karatoya; the infobox gives 1515 as the founding year and the State page gives Kamatapur as capital from 1515. He had removed the Baro-Bhuyan confederacy (his campaign began c. 1509). The pages give no area; the land between the two rivers is drawn as the Cooch Behar country, the Karatoya side and the Goalpara and Kamrup plains.
1562: 'The Barak valley was obtained by Chilarai in 1562' from the Twipra (Tripura) kingdom; he set up a garrison that became the Khaspur state (a Koch dewani).

ledger.note: 1581: the kingdom divides. 'This division occurred in 1581': at Barnagar near the Manas, Raghudev, Chilarai's son, takes the eastern portion (Koch Hajo, Hajo) and rules it 1581-1603; the Koch dynasty page agrees that Raghudev 'affected a split in the kingdom'. The Barak Valley, conquered by his father, is not named on any page; it is drawn with the eastern portion as a bridge. The State page dates Cooch Behar's own establishment to 1586, the year of Nara Narayan's death on that page.

wars.outcome: Mughal forces, allied with Lakshmi Narayan of Koch Bihar, attacked Parikshit Narayan of Koch Hajo in 1612; Koch Hajo was occupied by the end of that year and Parikshit was sent to Delhi (Koch dynasty page); the Koch Hajo page has the expedition leaving Dhaka in July 1612 and Parikshit driven to Pandu in 1614.
wars.note: The two pages differ on the end: 1612 (Koch dynasty page) or 1613-1614 (Koch Hajo page).

wars.outcome: A British-Koch coalition captured the capital in 1772; the British negotiated a peace with Bhutan on 25 April 1774 and Cooch Behar became a protectorate of the Company.
wars.note: The page gives the capture in 1772 and the peace of 25 April 1774; the protectorate years 1773-1858 are the infobox's.

certainty.note: The pages give the Karatoya and Barnadi as the limits, the Manas as the line of the 1581 split and no area; the shapes are discs round the Cooch Behar country and the Goalpara and Kamrup plains.
The final area (3,385 km2 in 1901) is known but the boundary is a disc; the Duars, held by Bhutan from the early 17th century and returned to British India in 1865, are not drawn.

notes:
Written 2026-10-25 by sa-06-x. A state Cliopatria lacks: cliopatria_names empty, four new keyframes. Four pages opened (Koch dynasty, Cooch Behar State, Kamata Kingdom, Koch Hajo); 'Koch Bihar State' failed (url_not_found). WebFetch returned extracts.

Scope: the dossier follows the Koch kingdom from Biswa Singha's proclamation in 1515 (capital Kamatapur from 1515 on the State page's infobox) rather than from the State page's 'Established 1586'; the 1581/1587 partition is a split to koch-hajo. Koch Hajo is written as its own dossier (koch-hajo) by this batch.

Disagreements: the split is 1581 (Koch Hajo page, Koch dynasty page) with Raghudev's independence in 1587 (both pages) and the State page's 1586 (Nara Narayan's death). Nara Narayan's reign is 1540-1586/87 on the Koch dynasty page and 1533-1587 on the State page. The merger is 1949 (State page text, Koch dynasty page) or 1 January 1950 (instrument of accession); the end year used is 1949. The Duars: 'from the early 17th century the Kingdom of Bhutan came to control the fertile plains' (State page) and in 1865 British India 'removed the Bhutanese influence from the Duars'; the State page does not say they were Cooch Behar's, so they are not drawn.

Page silent / not drawn: the extent under Nara Narayan (the Koch dynasty page lists Beltola, Rani and Dimarua as Kamrup states that gave allegiance and says the kingdom expanded 1510-1577, but no area), Jaintia, Cachar and Sylhet (not on the page), the Barak Valley after Chilarai (drawn with the eastern portion from 1581 as a bridge), the 1661 and 1707 infobox dates, the 1763-1765 reign of Debendra Narayan when 'Bhutan annexed land and its ambassador became de facto ruler' (no year; bhutan carries the 1765-1773 dependency as vassal_start/vassal_end of koch-bihar), the shrinkage of the state to its 3,385 km2 of 1901 other than the 1711 Mughal gains. The 1815-1949 history has no territorial event; the 1941 area is not on the pages.

Suzerainty (not in this ledger because vassal_start and vassal_end belong to the suzerain's dossier, counterpart = the vassal): 1609 Mughal vassal ('In 1609, Kuch Bihar became a vassal state of Mughal Empire'; Lakshmi Narayan submitted in person to Islam Khan in 1609, Koch Hajo page) for mughal-empire; 1664 pact of Pran Narayan with Shaista Khan; 1773 protectorate of the East India Company (infobox 1773-1858; recorded in east-india-company) and 1858-1947 British paramountcy (british-raj; the State page gives 1858 for the Raj and 'subject to overall British suzerainty' from 1775); 1949 merger (republic-of-india).

Cross-dossier: kingdom-of-tripura (the 1562 loss), koch-hajo, mughal-empire (the 1711 gain), kingdom-of-bhutan (carries koch-bihar 1765-1773), east-india-company, republic-of-india. Gazetteer: Cooch Behar, Boda, Patgram, Goalpara, Kamrup, the Barnadi, Karatoya and Manas rivers are absent; discs at 89.45 E 26.32 N (32 km), 88.6 E 26.45 N (28 km), 89.02 E 26.34 N (25 km), 90.6 E 26.2 N (70 km), 91.6 E 26.2 N (60 km) and the Barak Valley disc 92.65 E 24.75 N (60 km) are used.
